newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Reuters foreign exchange poll - Nov.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Reuters foreign exchange poll - Nov.

text.p: The dollar is expected to lose ground against the yen, slipping from current levels during November and accelerating lower thereafter, according to a Reuter poll of 40 banks and financial institutions from across the globe, conducted on November 5 and 6.

At 1220 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.5182/89 marks and 113.90/95 yen. Sterling/dollar was quoted at $1.6438/48, sterling/mark at 2.4965/80 and mark/yen at 74.95/98.
The minimum and maximum forecasts were as follows --

On average the forecasters expect dollar/yen to trade at 113.76 yen one month from now, easing to 112.95 in three months time before continuing its decline to trade at 110.26 in one year from now. The lowest dollar/yen is expected to fall during this period is 95.00 yen, the highest forecast for dollar/yen during this period is 125.00 yen.

The dollar is expected to be little changed against the mark over the next month to trade at 1.5196. It is then expected to pick up, rising to 1.5231 in three months and 1.5267 in six months before settling at 1.5262 in a year from now.
The net effect is forecasts for a much lower mark/yen.
The lowest dollar/mark is expected to fall during this period is 1.4000 marks and the highest it is expected to rise is 1.7000 marks.

The poll showed sterling is expected to decline steadily, weakening to $1.6396 one month from now and to weaken further to trade at $1.6192 one year from now. The lowest level sterling is expected to fall is to $1.5000, in a year from now.
Rankings of the 40 forecasters by the accuracy of their one-month forecasts will be published in the first week of December, just before the results of the next poll.
